For those who can't wait for the next patch release, here's a working workaround using the [Patch](https://github.com/amitfin/patch) custom integration from HACS.

The root cause is that `2026.5.3` ships with `renault-api==0.5.8` while `dev` has been bumped to `0.5.9` which fixes the authentication issue. The fix is to patch the `manifest.json` so Home Assistant installs the correct version.

**Steps:**

1. Install the [Patch](https://github.com/amitfin/patch) integration via HACS (add `amitfin/patch` as a custom repository, category: Integration) and restart HA.

2. Add the following to your `configuration.yaml`:

```yaml
patch:
  restart: true
  files:
    - destination: "{homeassistant}/components/renault/manifest.json"
      base: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/home-assistant/core/2026.5.3/homeassistant/components/renault/manifest.json
      patch: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/home-assistant/core/dev/homeassistant/components/renault/manifest.json
```

3. Restart Home Assistant. The integration will replace the `manifest.json` (bumping `renault-api` from `0.5.8` to `0.5.9`) and trigger an automatic restart, after which the Renault integration should authenticate successfully again.

Once the fix lands in an official patch release (e.g. `2026.5.4`), just remove the `patch:` block from `configuration.yaml` and restart — the workaround will cleanly remove itself.

> **Note:** The `patch` integration checks that the local file still matches the `base` before applying anything, so it won't silently break if the file changes in a future HA update.

items.body: ### The problem Built-in map now displays "API KEY REQUIRED" watermark from CARTO The problem Also reported in frontend - https://github.com/home-assistant/frontend/issues/53800 The default Home Assistant map is now displaying repeated "API KEY REQUIRED" watermarks across the map tiles. This appears to be caused by Home Assistant's frontend using CARTO's raster tile service without an API key: https://basemaps.cartocdn.com/rastertiles/voyager/{z}/{x}/{y}.png CARTO has recently started requiring an API key for these raster basemaps and is watermarking unauthenticated tile requests. The map itself still loads, but the watermark makes the built-in map look broken and significantly reduces usability. Expected behaviour The standard Home Assistant map should render normally without third-party API warning messages or watermarks. Suggested resolution Rather than adding a CARTO API key as a long-term fix, it may be worth reconsidering CARTO as the tile provider. The map already uses OpenStreetMap data, with CARTO acting only as the tile renderer/provider. CARTO also appears to be moving away from its legacy raster basemap service, so adding support for an API key may only postpone the problem. Possible options could include: moving to another suitable OpenStreetMap tile provider; moving to a vector-map implementation; introducing a configurable map/tile provider; or, as a short-term measure, supporting the required CARTO API key. Additional information The attribution currently shown on the map is: Leaflet | © OpenStreetMap, © CARTO This appears to affect the standard Home Assistant map implementation rather than a custom card or integration. 👋 Hey everyone, First things first: thank you. This thread got warm (in more ways than one 😅), but the feedback in here has been really useful, and I've read all of it. This is exactly how we make Home Assistant better, so please keep it coming. For real. Let me share where we are and what we're going to do about it. ## **A little context on the "why"** The area name showing up in generated entity IDs isn't a random change; it's one piece of a much larger, multi-year effort to clean up how naming works in Home Assistant. For a long time, all context (area, device, entity) had to be crammed into a single name, and that created a lot of duplication and maintenance pain. We've been moving toward naming every "thing" on its own, and letting Home Assistant provide the surrounding context where it's needed. That's a good direction, but I'll be honest with you: we clearly didn't get this particular step right for everyone, and that's on us to fix. ## **What we're going to do** Rather than a straight rollback, we're adding a setting to configure the entity ID format yourself. In short: * You'll be able to choose which parts are used (floor, area, device, entity) and in what order. If you'd rather not have the area in there, you can leave it out. * The current behavior stays the default, so nothing changes for you unless you want it to. This is how it looks (still in development): https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f13e19b-c1b4-4fac-a67d-6db815635861 ## **A few things I want to be really clear about** Because I've seen them come up a lot in here: * We do not change existing entity IDs. They live in the registry and they stay put. Your automations, scripts, scenes, and dashboards that reference them keep working. * This only applies when a new entity is first created, or when you deliberately regenerate an entity ID yourself. * Moving a device to another area does not rewrite its entity ID, exactly the same way that renaming a device or an entity has never changed it either. That's by design; silently rewriting IDs would break the things that point at them. * You can still rename any entity ID afterwards, right from its settings, just like today. * Some integrations set their own entity IDs (MQTT discovery, for example). Those keep using their preferred value. ## **A bit of general advice on naming going forward** If you're wondering how to best set things up, my honest advice is this: name every thing for what it is, on its own, and let Home Assistant add the context around it. * Give your floors, areas, devices, and entities short, standalone names. An area is "Living room", not "Ground floor living room". A device is "Multi sensor", not "Living room multi sensor". * Try not to repeat the area or device name further down the chain. Most of the double naming people run into (like `living_room_living_room_temperature`) comes from the same name being present twice. * Assign your devices to areas, and your areas to floors. That's what lets Home Assistant show the right context in pickers, dialogs, and tables, so you don't have to bake it into the names yourself. * If a card shows a name that's longer than you'd like, adjust the displayed name right on the card, or override it completely. That's the spot to tune how things read for you. The short version: you can let go of the old "cram everything into one name" strategies. Name things once, name them simply, and let the system fill in the rest. I'll be upfront that there are still a few gaps here; the History panel is one example where the context isn't shown as nicely yet. We're aware of those, and we expect to close them soon. ## **What about devices from hubs like Hue?** I know not all of this is in your hands. Some hubs and integrations (Philips Hue is the classic example) hand us devices that already have the room or area baked into the device name, so the area ends up showing twice through no fault of your own. We're adding handling for exactly that case: when you add a new device and its name starts with one of your existing area names (or an alias of it), Home Assistant will strip that prefix from the device name and preselect the matching area for you. It happens right there in the add-device dialog, so you can see what's going on and change it if you'd rather keep the name as is. ## **When?** The frontend and backend are basically ready (thank for the adhoc work, even in the late hours to the people involved). We're aiming to get this into 2026.8 (next major release). Please treat that as the target we are working toward rather than a hard promise, but that's where our head is at. I also want to be upfront that this is just one of the many steps, not the first step, and not the final word. There's more we want to do around naming to make the whole picture clearer, including an extensive blog post explaining it before we ship out the final pieces. Thanks again for caring enough to push on this. It genuinely helps 🙏 ../Frenck

                       

Blogging my personal ramblings at frenck.dev
